data.name: Id
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'idēs', meaning 'known' or 'recognized'. In the New Testament, Id is used in the name of the disciple named 'Judas Iscariot', who betrayed Jesus. The name Id symbolizes the human tendency to stray from faith and seek self-interest.

in_hebrew.name: עד
in_hebrew.long_meaning: One who comes to the aid, help, or support of another; a helper, supporter, or assistant; a companion, friend, or ally; an ally in battle or a confederate in a cause; a surety, pledge, or security for another's promise or obligation; an heir, successor, or representative.

in_greek.name: οἶδας
in_greek.long_meaning: From the verb 'oida', meaning 'to know' or 'to be acquainted with'; a name given to individuals who were wise or knowledgeable, or to those who were known or recognized by others.

in_latin.name: Idus
in_latin.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'idus', which is the past participle of the verb 'ideo', meaning 'to know' or 'to see'; a name given to individuals who were known or recognized by others.

in_english.name: Id
in_english.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English word 'id', meaning 'ego', 'I'; a name that signifies self-identity or self-awareness.

biblical_reference.note: The name 'Id' is not a biblical name.

data.cultural_impact: The name Id is most notably associated with Judas Iscariot, one of Jesus' twelve apostles who infamously betrayed Him. At the Last Supper, Judas agreed to betray Jesus to the religious authorities for thirty pieces of silver. Although there is no clear biblical reference to Judas having this name before the betrayal, a later tradition in Western Christianity adopted the name 'Judas Iscariot' due to its association with betrayal and deceit.
data.spiritual_significance: Id serves as a stark reminder of the human capacity for deceit and sin. It challenges us to strive for honesty and faithfulness in all areas of life. Judas' tragic story encourages us to reflect on the consequences of our actions and to remain true to our commitments - especially to our spiritual paths.
